extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting productive interviews between patent applicants (and their representatives) and USPTO examiners during patent prosecution, covering accessibility, preparation, substantive conduct, and recordation. Emphasizes procedures, timeliness, authority, materials to provide, and how to memorialize interview substance on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify identity and authority of interview participants
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting an interview, verify the individual assigned to represent the other party. An applicant should check the private Patent Application Information Retrieval (PAIR) system to identify the current examiner of record for a specific patent application. An examiner should check the record to confirm the interview requester has proper authority to act in the case on behalf of the principal or to act in a representative capacity with express authority from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PAIR to identify the examiner of record; examiners should confirm authority under 37 CFR 1.32 and MPEP 713.05. Note: a request from a representative without express authorization may still be granted (see Conducting an Interview with a Registered Practitioner Acting in a Representative Capacity, 1357 OG 254, Aug. 24, 2010; 37 CFR 1.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider examiner availability and timing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are reminded that examiner availability for interviews may be limited during the weeks leading up to the end of each fiscal quarter (generally the weeks leading up to December 31st, March 31st, June 30th, and September 30th).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule interviews with awareness of fiscal-quarter staffing limitations and avoid last-minute requests near quarter-ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request interviews early, especially for in-person meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit a request for an interview as early as possible, particularly when an in-person interview is being requested, to ensure the examiner of record and/or an examiner with negotiating authority will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early requests increase the likelihood that the examiner and appropriate authority can attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient notice and a proposed agenda using PTOL-413A/B
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for an interview should be given to the other party with sufficient notice, including a proposed agenda, to allow for sufficient preparation. Applicants should use form PTOL-413A and examiners should use form PTOL-413B for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the general intent/goal of the interview and a brief summary of arguments on PTOL-413A/B so the other side can prepare effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and cooperative in scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the applicant and the examiner should be flexible in attempting to arrange a mutually convenient date and time for an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for mutually agreeable times and consider grouping interviews where effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to voicemail and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: In the ordinary course of business, both the applicant and the examiner should strive to reply to voicemail messages within one business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely replies reduce delays in prosecution and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide helpful voicemail greetings and alternate contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorded voicemail greetings and voicemail messages should include helpful information such as the availability and/or unavailability of each party, applicable time zone, and contact information for alternate personnel who can provide assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary voicemail greetings during extended absence should include date of return and contact information for alternate personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant interviews that develop or clarify outstanding issues and manage time efficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be granted or continued when the nature of the case is such that the interview serves to develop or clarify outstanding issues in an application. Both applicants and examiners should understand that interview time is limited for both parties, and use interview time efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure interviews do not extend beyond a reasonable time, minimize interruptions, do not abruptly end, and facilitate grouping of interviews when effective (MPEP 713.01 III; 713.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform the Office of related cases and request grouped assignment when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should inform the Office of all related cases (continuations, CIPs, divisionals) and, if deemed appropriate, the Office should assign related cases to the same examiner to promote grouped interviewing of related applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping related cases with the same examiner promotes efficiency and consistent handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed agenda and materials well in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should receive a detailed agenda along with any proposed amendments, arguments or evidence as far in advance of the interview as possible. The more lead time the examiner has to consider the amendments or arguments before the interview, the greater the likelihood of a successful interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include a general intent/goal and brief summary of arguments using PTOL-413A; provide proposed amendments, citations to the specification supporting amendments, citations to portions of references to be discussed, and any additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should be prepared to explain claim and prior art interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should be prepared to explain how the applied prior art is being interpreted, how the claims are being interpreted, and how the applied art discloses each limitation of the claims for which the art is being relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear articulation of mapping between claim limitations and prior art elements helps productive discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant should explain inventive concept and distinctions from prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be prepared to explain the 'inventive concept' of the invention and any differences between the prior art of record and the claims, as previously presented and/or amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the inventive concept is captured in the claims and how claims are distinguished over the prior art; avoid over-focusing on minor/trivial details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit proposed responses and amendments before interview when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, applicants should submit a proposed response in advance of the interview to allow examiners sufficient time to prepare and conduct a well organized interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed response should include all proposed amendments to specification, claims and drawings, citations to spec support for amendments, citations to reference portions to be discussed, additional evidence, and a brief summary of arguments. A fully 37 CFR 1.111-compliant submission is unnecessary prior to the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review of materials prior to interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should review any proposed amendments, arguments and/or evidence prior to conducting an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-interview review increases the chances the interview will identify resolution paths and be efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure examiner has negotiating/signatory authority or involve supervisory examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should at least have negotiating authority for the interview and, if the examiner does not have signatory authority, the examiner should include a primary/supervisory examiner in the interview (in person or by telephone) or at least consult a primary/supervisory examiner before conducting the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If post-interview reversal of any agreement occurs, the primary/supervisory examiner should promptly call the applicant to discuss and/or arrange a follow-up interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant representative should obtain applicant approval and negotiating authority
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's representative should consult with the applicant prior to the interview to discuss the invention and all relevant current issues and obtain applicant approval and/or negotiating authority to accept at least a range of reasonably foreseeable proposals that may arise during an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the examiner in advance if the representative does not have negotiating authority, as interviews are not normally granted unless the party has sufficient authority (MPEP 713.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-fill Interview Summary form (PTOL-413/PTOL-413B) where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the interview, for efficiency and where appropriate, the examiner should fill out the top portion of the Interview Summary form PTOL-413 or PTOL-413B, including identifying the rejections, claims and prior art documents to be discussed and optionally the interview participants, date, and type of interview, and bring a copy of this form to the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling out the form in advance streamlines the interview and recordation process (MPEP 713.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and communicate any new issues before interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners and applicants should identify any new issues with the case not already of record before conducting the interview and communicate them to each other along with any questions that may arise during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forewarned issues allow preparation and avoid surprises that waste interview time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thoroughly conversant with the case record
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the examiner and the applicant should be thoroughly conversant with the specification, claims, relevant prior art, all grounds of rejection, relevant arguments and issues currently of record in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough familiarity is necessary to identify allowable subject matter and meaningfully advance prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek to resolve as many outstanding issues as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the examiner and the applicant should look for opportunities to resolve as many outstanding issues as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be used proactively to narrow disputes and identify allowable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide real-world examples to aid examiner understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be prepared to identify 'real world' applications of the claimed invention to assist in enhancing the examiner's understanding of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete application examples can clarify claim scope and inventive concept for examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct interviews cooperatively and not as adversaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners and applicants should not conduct interviews as adversaries, but rather, should conduct interviews with the objective of meeting the common goals of advancing prosecution and resolving issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cooperative posture facilitates productive exchange and problem-solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand that interview agreements may be provisional pending final searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should appreciate that even if agreement is reached regarding patentability during an interview, an examiner will perform a final update and interference search, which can produce prior art that negates the patentability agreement reached in the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume interview agreements are final until the examiner completes final checks (MPEP 719.05, 904 and 1302.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide introductory summary when a new examiner joins
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner of record participating in the interview is new to the case, at the beginning of the interview, applicant should provide the new examiner an introductory summary/discussion of the invention, referencing the claims, specification and figures, to the extent necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise orientation brings new examiners up to speed and makes the interview productive (MPEP 713.01 V).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specification support for proposed claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing claim amendments, both the examiner and the applicant should identify support in the specification for the proposed claim amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly linking amendments to spec support reduces later written-record problems and §112 issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should help identify allowable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should evaluate the claims over the prior art and assist the applicant in identifying allowable subject matter. Both the examiner and applicant should cooperatively work toward identifying allowable subject matter, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should suggest allowable subject matter when satisfied that the prior art has been fully developed (MPEP 707.07(j) III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interviews to advance prosecution, not repeat prior positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties should refrain from using an interview to re-present the same positions previously presented and addressed and instead utilize the interview to further advance prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus discussion on new steps toward resolution rather than restating prior submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to explain rationale for positions taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the examiner and the applicant should be prepared to explain the rationale for any positions taken during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the examiner should articulate why a proposed amendment does not overcome a rejection; the applicant should explain why examiner-suggested amendments are unacceptable (e.g., too narrow in light of prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure mutual understanding of claim language and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider addressing claim language, semantics, conjunctions, punctuation, etc.; consider reading a claim out loud; consider diagramming the elements of the claim and their interrelationships to determine claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical techniques (reading aloud, diagramming) help parties converge on claim meaning and avoid misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorialize interviews in writing on the record
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral discussions between applicants and examiners must be summarized in a writing on the record to satisfy the USPTO requirement that all business be transacted in writing. No agreements, promises, stipulations or understandings will be recognized that are not on the written record in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All interview substance affecting prosecution must appear in written form on the record (37 CFR 1.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand that agendas and proposed amendments become part of the record
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are reminded that, according to USPTO policy, agendas and proposed amendments submitted by any means to the Office, including facsimile or email communications will be retained as a record by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions via email, facsimile, EFS-Web, etc., are preserved (see USPTO Internet Usage Policy; EFS-Web legal framework; MPEP references). Consider the potential adverse impact of unpersuasive proposed amendments being on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: All merit discussions are considered interviews and will be made of record
rubrics_metrics.description: According to USPTO policy, all discussions between the applicant/practitioner and the examiner regarding the merits of a pending application will be considered an interview and will be made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat any substantive meritorious communication as part of the interview record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve time to agree what will be included in Interview Summary Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Time should be reserved at the end of a personal or telephonic interview to discuss what should be included in an Interview Summary Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the end of the interview to confirm the content that will be put on the PTOL-413 to avoid later disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for a complete Interview Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete and proper recordation of the substance of an interview, by both applicant and the examiner, should include the items listed in MPEP 713.04 including a brief identification of each argument or issue discussed, indication of any other pertinent matters discussed regarding patentability, the results or outcome of the interview, and an indication as to whether or not agreement was reached on the issues raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP 713.04 checklist: identify arguments/issues, other pertinent patentability matters, results/outcome, and whether agreement was reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant expected to provide separate interview summary unless waived in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though an examiner completes a PTOL-413 Interview Summary form, applicant is expected to provide a separate summary of the interview unless the examiner indicates in writing on the PTOL-413 that a written summary of the interview by the applicant is not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should prepare their own written summary unless explicitly waived by the examiner on the PTOL-413.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should review applicant's interview summary for accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant's record of the substance of an interview to ensure the record is complete and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt examiner review helps ensure the official record reflects the true substance and outcome of the interview (MPEP 713.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of suitable interview summary content
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable interview summary comments capture the thrust of issues/arguments raised in an interview using concrete references (example items include: applicant argued a reference combination does not render the invention obvious with pinpoint citations; applicant argued examiner's claim-term interpretation is unreasonably broad with specification citations; agreement that material incorporated by reference is necessary and applicant must amend specification; specific proposed amendment discussed with detailed edits and limitations noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise statements with citations to specification pages/columns/lines and identify specific claim limitations, statutory bases (§112, §101, obviousness), and actions required. These examples illustrate the level of specificity required to be 'suitable' (see Example A list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of unsuitable interview summary content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unsuitable interview summary comments are vague and do not capture the thrust of the issues/arguments (examples: 'Issues of Anticipation/Obviousness were discussed'; 'Agreement was (or was not) reached because the claims are found patentable (or unpatentable)'; generic restatements that do not identify specifics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid one-line or generic summaries that omit citations, specific claim language, or the nature of the dispute. The 'unsuitable' list provides anti-patterns to avoid in interview summaries.
